input.quote: 14.1 Indemnification by RevMed. RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees ("Sanofi Indemnitees") from and against any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement against any of them to the extent arising or resulting from:
input.rationale: Section 14.1 already gives us a defend-and-indemnify obligation from RevMed for Sanofi and its Affiliates covering RevMed's negligence, recklessness and willful misconduct and its material breaches of warranties and obligations (which, read with the Section 13.4(b) covenant to comply with all Applicable Law, captures RevMed's breach of law), and Section 14.3 supplies notice, control of the defence and cooperation. What is absent is any intellectual-property limb: no provision indemnifies us against allegations that the licensed technology or our exercise of the granted licences infringes or misappropriates Third Party IP, and Section 13.5 expressly disclaims any non-infringement warranty while Section 10.7 merely obliges the Parties to negotiate a Third Party licence. That is the walk-away case of no Vendor IP indemnity, so the clause fails the fallback. We therefore target the preferred position: express IP infringement/misappropriation and unauthorised-access/disclosure limbs in Section 14.1 (using the defined term "RevMed Licensed Technology", Section 1.99), a conforming "(a) through (e)" cross-reference, and narrowing of our own Section 14.2 indemnity to Sanofi-provided content and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law. We decline the fallback because its 3x annual-fees super-cap would cap an indemnity that is currently uncapped (Section 14.5 preserves indemnity claims) and "annual fees" has no analogue in this upfront/milestone/royalty structure.

proposal.summary: Add express RevMed IP-infringement and data-breach indemnity limbs to Section 14.1 and narrow Sanofi's indemnity under Section 14.2 to Sanofi-provided materials and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] RevMed's indemnity does not reach Third Party intellectual property claims and Section 13.5 disclaims any non-infringement warranty, so we have added a limb indemnifying us against allegations that the RevMed Licensed Technology or our exercise of the licenses infringes or misappropriates Third Party intellectual property, plus a limb for unauthorized access to or disclosure of Sanofi data, and conformed the Section 14.1 cross-reference. Consistent with our position that our own indemnity stays narrow, we have limited Section 14.2 to Sanofi-provided content and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law.

(c) the material breach of any of the warranties or representations made by Sanofi to RevMed under this Agreement or any Ancillary Agreement; or
(d) the material breach by Sanofi of any of its obligations pursuant to this Agreement or any Ancillary Agreement;
